options.name: White Tank Mountain Regional Park (Willow/semi-developed sites)
options.priceNote: $25/night semi-developed (walk-in tent sites); developed W/E sites $40; +$10 non-refundable reservation fee. Fees current per Maricopa County schedule effective Jan 1, 2026. Park entry fee $10/vehicle (cyclists typically pay a small bike entry fee).
options.locationNote: ~11-12 mi SW of Sun City West via Citrus Rd + Olive Ave to White Tank Mountain Rd — a real detour, all suburban/rural roads
options.legalityNote: Established Maricopa County regional park campground — fully legal
options.cyclistIntel: Standard Phoenix-area cyclist camp; quiet in early Nov. Big detour off the ST line is the only downside.
options.seasonalNote: Early Nov is prime season in the Phoenix area; weekends can book up — reserve

options.name: Lake Pleasant Regional Park
options.priceNote: $25/night semi-developed, $40 developed; +$10 reservation fee (same Maricopa County fee schedule, effective Jan 2026); entry fee extra
options.locationNote: ~15-17 mi NE of Sun City West via Lake Pleasant Pkwy — wrong direction from the westbound route
options.cyclistIntel: Adjacent private Pleasant Harbor RV Resort is RV/boat-oriented — not the budget/tent play; the county park is
options.seasonalNote: Snowbird season ramping up in Nov; reserve

bestBet: White Tank Mountain Regional Park (Willow/semi-developed sites)
gapAdvice: Sun City West itself has zero tent camping — the 55+ RV resorts (e.g., in Sun City/Surprise) don't take tents. Nearest legal camping is White Tank Mountain Regional Park, an ~11-12 mi detour SW. If you don't want to add ~22-24 mi round trip to tomorrow's 73-mi day, take a budget motel in Surprise on the route (Motel 6 / Days Inn cluster on Grand Ave/US-60, typically $60-85 in Nov) and bank the sleep.

options.name: Gladden Trailer & RV Park
options.priceNote: Rate unpublished; monthly/seasonal-oriented park. Tent policy UNVERIFIED — call/ask before relying on it. No listed phone; park is on US-60 at Aguila (find via Facebook or ask at Aguila Family Dollar).
options.locationNote: 0.1 mi off route on US-60 at Aguila
options.legalityNote: Private RV park — legal with permission; under new ownership, no longer Escapees-affiliated, confirmed accepting short-term stays (4.8-star recent reviews)
options.cyclistIntel: The classic Aguila stop, Burro Jim Motel, is CLOSED (Yelp, Oct 2025) — this park is effectively the only roof/camp at the day's end point

options.name: Horspitality RV Park
options.priceNote: Tent rate unpublished (park listed as pricier RV resort) — 9 dedicated tents-only sites confirmed; call for the tent rate, likely $25-40
options.locationNote: On US-60 ~4 mi SE of downtown Wickenburg — directly on route, but ~25-28 mi BEFORE Aguila (shortens the day)
options.legalityNote: Private all-ages RV park with 9 tents-only sites (AllStays) — legal
options.cyclistIntel: Southern Tier riders have stayed here since at least 2007 (Drew Bratton's CGOAB journal). Note Wickenburg's Constellation Park ($10 city camping) is self-contained-RVs-ONLY — no tents.
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; snowbirds arriving in Nov — call ahead

gapAdvice: Aguila is the thinnest night of this segment: Burro Jim Motel is closed, Constellation Park (Wickenburg) bans tents, and there's no named BLM dispersed area at Aguila (US-60 corridor here is private ag + state trust land, which needs an AZ permit). Plan A: confirm tents at Gladden before leaving Wickenburg. Plan B: stop at Horspitality RV Park near Wickenburg (mi ~2464) and eat the 28-mi shift into tomorrow (Quartzsite day becomes ~88 mi — flat). Plan C: ask at the Aguila community church/school ballfield — small-town courtesy camping is common ST practice, but get explicit permission. Water: buy at Aguila's Family Dollar.

options.name: Dome Rock BLM 14-Day Camping Area
options.priceNote: FREE — get the free 14-day permit from the seasonal camp host at the entrance
options.locationNote: S of I-10 at Dome Rock Rd exit, ~3 mi W of Quartzsite — essentially ON route as you leave town westbound (mi 2553.4)
options.legalityNote: Fully legal BLM 14-day free dispersed area with camp-host registration — the budget backbone of Quartzsite
options.cyclistIntel: 400 sites, camp anywhere in the boundary; hard flat desert, easy tent pitching. Load ALL water in Quartzsite (3 mi east) — zero facilities here.
options.seasonalNote: Early Nov = start of snowbird season; plenty of space (the crush is Jan-Feb gem show)

options.name: Hi Jolly BLM 14-Day Camping Area
options.locationNote: ~2 mi N of Main St on US-95 N — short off-route detour the wrong direction; Dome Rock is the better free pick westbound
options.legalityNote: Legal BLM free 14-day dispersed area, ~100 sites

options.name: B-10 Campground (B10 RV Park & Campground)
options.priceNote: Reported $25/night (W/E) to $40; ~20-40 dedicated tent sites — call for current tent rate. Worth it if you want a SHOWER.
options.locationNote: 615 W Main St, downtown Quartzsite — on route (mi ~2550.7-2552.3)
options.legalityNote: Private campground that explicitly welcomes tents (rare in Quartzsite — 88 Shades and most others are RV-only)
options.cyclistIntel: Walking distance to all Quartzsite services; open Oct 1-Mar 31 so it IS open Nov 4
options.seasonalNote: Seasonal Oct-Mar — open for your date

options.name: La Posa LTVA (West/North/South)
options.priceNote: In LTVA season (Sept 15-Apr 15) the cheapest legal permit is the $40 short-visit permit covering any 14 consecutive days — poor value for ONE night; season permit $180. Fees confirmed unchanged for 2025-26 (proposed $600 hike did NOT go through). The $15/night rate only applies off-season (Apr 16-Sept 14).
options.locationNote: ~2 mi S of town on US-95 S (mi 2550.7-2551.1 per OSM)
options.legalityNote: Legal BLM LTVA; tents explicitly permitted. Permit sold on site.
options.cyclistIntel: Only worth $40 if you want the amenities: 8 potable water faucets, vault toilets, dump, trash. For one tent night, Dome Rock free beats it.
options.seasonalNote: Nov 4 is inside LTVA season, so short-visit permit pricing applies

options.name: Hippie Hole Camping Area (BLM)
options.priceNote: Listed as free dispersed camping; some maps place it inside the local BLM fee program — carry $15 cash in case
options.locationNote: ~3 mi from Palo Verde on the Colorado River, dirt-road access off route
options.legalityNote: BLM-managed river camping area — legal, but verify locally whether the fee envelope applies
options.cyclistIntel: River access = swim/rinse; can be a local party spot on weekends (Nov 5, 2026 is a Thursday — should be quiet)

options.name: Palo Verde County Park
options.priceNote: $15/night ($7.50 with America the Beautiful pass; $75 annual). NOT free anymore despite older reports.
options.locationNote: On CA-78 ~2 mi S of Palo Verde store — effectively ON route (tomorrow's direction of travel), mi ~2600.7
options.legalityNote: Established county park campground, ~18-20 first-come sites — legal
options.cyclistIntel: Flush toilets, tables, fire rings, shade ramadas, 14-day limit. NO drinking water — buy at the Palo Verde store/bar 2 mi back before rolling in.
options.seasonalNote: Snowbird arrivals begin in Nov but midweek space is near-certain

options.name: Oxbow Campground (BLM)
options.priceNote: $15/night overnight fee, envelope pay ($7.50 with America the Beautiful pass; $75 annual covers area BLM fee sites)
options.locationNote: 0.6 mi off route at mi 2598.7, on the Colorado River oxbow
options.legalityNote: Legal BLM fee campground with host in season
options.cyclistIntel: River setting, vault toilets, no potable water — same drill: stock up in Palo Verde
options.seasonalNote: Popular with anglers/snowbirds from Nov on

options.name: Tamarisk Mobile Home Park & Campground
options.priceNote: Rate UNKNOWN — could not verify via any 2024-2026 source; OSM tags it 'Cyclists Welcome' which usually traces to ACA map data, so it likely hosts ST riders — ask at the office
options.locationNote: OSM places it at mi 2594.3 on CA-78 just N of Palo Verde
options.legalityNote: Private park — legal with permission only
options.cyclistIntel: Unverified beyond the OSM/ACA tag; treat as a bonus, not a plan

options.name: Wiest Lake County Park
options.priceNote: ~$30/night per recent camper reports; Imperial County publishes no online rate card — call (442) 265-1736 to confirm current tent rate
options.locationNote: 5351 Dietrich Rd — ~6 mi N of Brawley via CA-111 N + Rutherford Rd; a real detour off the day's end point
options.legalityNote: Imperial County officially lists both RV and TENT camping here — legal and current (county Public Works page)
options.cyclistIntel: Lakeside grass, charcoal grills (no ground fires), clean bathrooms with showers per reviews — the only real tent camping in the Brawley area
options.seasonalNote: Imperial Valley camping season is winter — open and pleasant in Nov

options.name: Imperial Sand Dunes Rec Area (Glamis) — BLM
options.priceNote: Permit fees ROSE Oct 1, 2025: $55/week off-site, $70/week on-site, $185/season, charged per street-legal 'primary vehicle' Oct 1-Apr 15. A bicycle is an edge case rangers may wave through, but don't bank on it
options.locationNote: Route passes Glamis at ~mi 2640, 26 mi before Brawley
options.legalityNote: Legal BLM camping with permit, but it's an OHV mega-area — camps are RV/toy-hauler flats
options.cyclistIntel: NOT recommended: weekly-permit pricing is terrible value for one tent night, zero water, and Nov weekends bring wall-to-wall OHV noise. Push on to Brawley.
options.seasonalNote: Nov 6, 2026 is a Friday — the dunes will be filling up with OHV crowds that evening

gapAdvice: Brawley proper has no tent camping — Palm Lane RV Park is RVs-only. Wiest Lake means ~6 extra miles north (and 6 back south in the morning). If you won't ride the detour after a 68-mi dunes day, take a budget motel on Brawley's Main St/CA-86 (typically $70-95). Skip Glamis camping — the new $55+ weekly vehicle permits and Friday-night OHV chaos make it the worst deal on this segment.

options.name: Desert Trails RV Park & Golf Course
options.priceNote: ~$37/night W/E sites reported (one caller quoted $45); ~100 tent sites per directory listings — call 760-352-7275 for the actual tent rate, which may come in under $35
options.locationNote: 225 Wake Ave, south El Centro — on/near route at ~mi 2684, i.e. ~10 mi BEFORE the Calexico end point
options.legalityNote: Private RV park that accepts tents (one of very few in Imperial Valley) — legal
options.cyclistIntel: Showers, laundry, pool; last realistic camp before the border. Camp here and roll the final flat 10 mi into Calexico in the morning.
options.seasonalNote: Winter-season park — fully open in Nov, snowbirds arriving

bestBet: Desert Trails RV Park & Golf Course
gapAdvice: Calexico itself has zero legal camping. Nearby 'options' all fail for tents: Sunbeam Lake RV Resort is RVs-only (300 sites, no tents), Rio Bend RV & Golf Resort is resort-priced with no published tent sites, and Country Life RV Park (mi 2683.2) could not be verified as tent-friendly. Real choices: (1) camp Desert Trails in El Centro at mi ~2684 and finish the last 10 mi next morning, or (2) budget motel in Calexico — several independents plus chains along Imperial Ave (SR-111), typically $65-95 in Nov; El Centro's Motel 6/chain cluster off I-8 runs similar. Book the border-town motel ahead on a Saturday night (Nov 7).
